# Context

**Package** `telividb.context.v1`

## Services

### `ContextTemplates`

Manages context templates and assembles retrieval context from them.  Named for the resource it manages rather than for the operation, which is both what AIP-121 asks and what avoids a real collision: a service called `Context` generates a trait called `Context`, and that shadows `std::task::Context` inside the generated service code.  The boundary is deliberate: this returns ranked, deduplicated, budget-fitted fragments with provenance. It does not render a prompt and does not call a generative model. The moment the engine templates prompts it is coupled to one model's chat format, and the database would need re-releasing every time a template changed.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CreateContextTemplate` | `CreateContextTemplateRequest` | `ContextTemplate` | Creates a context template. |
| `GetContextTemplate` | `GetContextTemplateRequest` | `ContextTemplate` | Retrieves a single context template. |
| `ListContextTemplates` | `ListContextTemplatesRequest` | `ListContextTemplatesResponse` | Lists context templates. |
| `DeleteContextTemplate` | `DeleteContextTemplateRequest` | `ContextTemplate` | Soft-deletes a context template. |
| `AssembleContext` | `AssembleContextRequest` | `AssembleContextResponse` | Searches, expands along the graph, deduplicates, ranks and fits a budget. Unary rather than streaming. Streaming would change the ranking contract: you cannot re-rank what has already been sent, and the whole value here is that the ordering accounts for everything retrieved. |

### `ContextTemplate`

A saved retrieval configuration.  A resource rather than a set of request parameters, because it is also an authorization surface: the person who saves a template and the person who runs it may see different rows. Policy is therefore evaluated at run time against the caller, never at save time against the author — otherwise a saved template becomes a way to read rows you could not query for directly.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the template. |
| `display_name` | `string` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | Human-readable name. |
| `expansion` | `Expansion` | 3 | `OPTIONAL` | How far to expand along the graph. |
| `budget` | `Budget` | 4 | `OPTIONAL` | Ceiling on what may be returned. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 5 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the template was created. |
| `update_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the template was last modified. |
| `delete_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the template was soft-deleted, or unset while live. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When a soft-deleted template is purged and becomes unrecoverable. |
| `etag` | `string` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

### `Expansion`

How far a retrieval expands from its similarity seeds.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_hop_count` | `int32` | 1 | `OPTIONAL` | Hops to follow. Zero disables expansion and returns pure similarity. |
| `edge_types` | `repeated string` | 2 | `OPTIONAL` | Edge types to follow. Empty follows every non-structural type. |
| `decay` | `float` | 3 | `OPTIONAL` | Per-hop score multiplier. |
| `max_expanded_count` | `int32` | 4 | `OPTIONAL` | Ceiling on expanded results, so a hub cannot become the whole answer. |
| `use_strength` | `bool` | 5 | `OPTIONAL` | Whether learned traversal strength contributes to ranking. |
| `use_summaries` | `bool` | 6 | `OPTIONAL` | Whether to search the summary tier before the message tier. Coarse-to-fine: summaries narrow the field, then expansion descends into the messages they cover. The same shape the vector path already uses when a quantized scan precedes a full-precision rerank. |

### `Budget`

A ceiling on what an assembly may return.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_fragment_count` | `int32` | 1 | `OPTIONAL` | Maximum fragments to return. |
| `max_token_count` | `int32` | 2 | `OPTIONAL` | Approximate token ceiling across all fragments. |

### `Fragment`

One retrieved piece of context, with the path that reached it.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | 1 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | The resource this came from. |
| `content` | `string` | 2 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | The text. |
| `score` | `float` | 3 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Combined score after similarity, decay, weights and recency. |
| `hop_count` | `int32` | 4 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Hops from the nearest seed. Zero means a direct similarity match. |
| `reached_via` | `string` | 5 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | The seed this was reached from. |
| `summarized` | `bool` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Whether this fragment is a summary rather than stored content. |
| `mcp_server` | `string` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | The MCP server this originated with, when it came from a tool result. Provenance carried through to the point of use: text a third-party server returned must not rank as memory the same way something a person said does, and a caller cannot make that distinction without being told. |
